ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: Urban History Description: This course examines urban history through the dynamic history of the Black urban Midwest, with a focus on Chicago and St. Louis. Transnational and intersectional in breadth, students will come to appreciate the importance of the Midwest to the African American experience and to the making of the modern world. Topics include racial capitalism, settler colonialism, white supremacy, empire, migration, space, women, sexualities, slavery, freedom, culture, industrialization, deindustrialization, gentrification, Black Lives Matter, and Covid-19. Students will write a research paper based on original research on a topic of their choice related to African American Midwestern urban history. A premium will be placed on teaching students how to conduct primary research, namely utilizing archival sources, newspaper, and oral histories. If you are serious about learning and in thinking in new directions, then this class is for you.
